heading: INT. ROOFTOP GREENHOUSE, LAUNDROMAT BUILDING - DUSK

units.text: INT. ROOFTOP GREENHOUSE, LAUNDROMAT BUILDING - DUSK
Cracked glass panes.
Tomato vines grown wild.
A rusted fan turns without wind.
Laundry lines sag with sheets, still dripping.
MIRIAM STOLZ-AGYEMAN (60s, silver bun, gardening gloves) trims a vine.
Her son WENDELL (30s, work boots, tie loosened) sits on an upturned bucket.
His wife TOVA (30s, pregnant, hand on her belly) leans in the doorway.
Their neighbor, old CASPIAN DRUMMOND (80s, oxygen tank, tiny sunhat), dozes in a lawn chair.
Landlord says we have until Friday.
units.name: MIRIAM

units.text: Mom.
units.name: WENDELL

units.text: Friday. That's four days.
units.name: MIRIAM

units.text: We'll find another roof.
units.name: TOVA

units.text: Another roof won't have these.
units.name: MIRIAM

units.text: She holds up a tomato, ripe and enormous.
Wendell looks at it, then at his wife.
Beefsteak.
units.name: CASPIAN

units.text: Cranberry heirloom.
units.name: MIRIAM

units.text: Beefsteak.
units.name: CASPIAN

units.text: Miriam sighs and places the tomato in Tova's hand.
Tova weighs it, smiling.
It's heavy.
units.name: TOVA

units.text: Mom, you can't carry this up the stairs forever.
units.name: WENDELL

units.text: Watch me.
units.name: MIRIAM
